subject: maths
prompt_en: Problem A: buses leave every 6 and every 8 minutes, together now; when are they next together? Problem B: 18 boys and 24 girls stand in equal rows of only boys or only girls; what is the biggest row size? Which needs common factors and which common multiples?
prompt_hi: Problem A: buses har 6 aur har 8 minute mein chalti hain, abhi saath chali; agli baar saath kab? Problem B: 18 ladke aur 24 ladkiyan barabar rows mein khade hain, row mein sirf ladke ya sirf ladkiyan; sabse badi row kitni? Kisme common factors chahiye aur kisme common multiples?
answer: A needs common multiples (24 minutes); B needs common factors (6 per row)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Two temple bells ring every 4 minutes and every 10 minutes. They ring together at 9:00. When do they next ring together?
prompt_hi: Mandir ki do ghantiyan har 4 minute aur har 10 minute mein bajti hain. 9:00 baje saath bajti hain. Agli baar saath kab bajengi?

subject: maths
prompt_en: A shopkeeper has 24 pens and 36 pencils. He wants identical gift packs that use all of them. What is the largest number of packs, and what goes in each?
prompt_hi: Ek dukaandaar ke paas 24 pen aur 36 pencil hain. Woh ek jaise gift packs banana chahta hai jinme saare lag jaayein. Sabse zyada kitne packs, aur har pack mein kya?
answer: 12 packs, each with 2 pens and 3 pencils

subject: maths
prompt_en: On a number line from 0 to 30 you jump in 3s and a friend jumps in 5s. Where do you both land?
prompt_hi: 0 se 30 tak ki number line pe tum 3-3 ki jump lagate ho aur dost 5-5 ki. Dono kahan-kahan same jagah utarte ho?
answer: 15 and 30 (and the start, 0)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Teach a friend the difference between factors and multiples using the number 4.
prompt_hi: 4 ka example lekar dost ko factors aur multiples ka fark sikhao.
answer: Factors of 4 (1, 2, 4) divide 4 exactly and are few; multiples of 4 (4, 8, 12, …) are in its table and never end

subject: maths
prompt_en: Quick! Which number is a factor of every number?
prompt_hi: Jaldi! Kaunsa number har number ka factor hai?

subject: maths
prompt_en: Is 21 prime or composite?
prompt_hi: 21 prime hai ya composite?
answer: Composite (21 = 3 × 7)

subject: maths
prompt_en: 91 is odd and looks like a prime. Predict, then check: is it prime?
prompt_hi: 91 odd hai aur prime jaisa lagta hai. Pehle guess karo, phir check karo: kya yeh prime hai?

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why is 1 not a prime number?
prompt_hi: 1 prime number kyon nahi hai?
answer: It has only one factor, itself; a prime must have exactly two different factors

subject: maths
prompt_en: Try arranging 7 chairs in equal rows, with more than one row and more than one chair per row. Then try 8 chairs. What is the difference?
prompt_hi: 7 kursiyon ko barabar rows mein lagao, ek se zyada row aur har row mein ek se zyada kursi. Phir 8 kursiyon ke saath karo. Kya fark hai?
answer: 7 cannot be done (only 1 row of 7), so 7 is prime; 8 can be 2 rows of 4, so 8 is composite

subject: maths
prompt_en: Ayaan says, '2 can't be prime, because prime numbers are odd.' Correct him.
prompt_hi: Ayaan kehta hai, '2 prime nahi ho sakta, kyunki prime numbers odd hote hain.' Usse theek karo.
answer: 2 has exactly two factors, 1 and 2, so it is prime; it is the only even prime

subject: maths
prompt_en: In the sieve up to 100, after crossing out multiples of 2, 3, 5 and 7, which numbers in the 40s survive?
prompt_hi: 100 tak ki sieve mein 2, 3, 5 aur 7 ke multiples kaatne ke baad 40s mein kaun se numbers bachte hain?

subject: maths
prompt_en: In the sieve up to 100, why can we stop after crossing out the multiples of 7?
prompt_hi: 100 tak ki sieve mein 7 ke multiples kaatne ke baad hum ruk kyon sakte hain?
answer: Any composite up to 100 has a factor no bigger than 10 (since 11 × 11 = 121 > 100), so it was already crossed out by 2, 3, 5 or 7

subject: maths
prompt_en: Is 57 prime?
prompt_hi: Kya 57 prime hai?

subject: maths
prompt_en: A teacher wants to seat 29 children in equal rows, with more than one row and more than one child in each row. Can she? What about 30 children?
prompt_hi: Ek teacher 29 bachchon ko barabar rows mein bithana chahti hai, ek se zyada row aur har row mein ek se zyada bachcha. Kya ho sakta hai? Aur 30 bachche hon toh?
answer: No for 29, because it is prime; yes for 30, e.g. 5 rows of 6

subject: maths
prompt_en: Make 12 square tiles into rectangles in every possible way. How many different rectangles, and what does that tell you?
prompt_hi: 12 square tiles se har tarah ke rectangles banao. Kitne alag rectangles bante hain, aur isse kya pata chalta hai?
answer: 3: 1 × 12, 2 × 6, 3 × 4; more than one way means 12 is composite

subject: maths
prompt_en: Teach a friend how to tell a prime from a composite, and warn them about two traps.
prompt_hi: Dost ko sikhao prime aur composite mein fark kaise karein, aur do traps se saavdhan karo.
answer: Count the factors: exactly 2 means prime, more than 2 means composite. Traps: 1 is neither; odd does not mean prime (9, 15, 21); and 2 is prime

subject: maths
prompt_en: Quick! Name the prime numbers between 10 and 20.
prompt_hi: Jaldi! 10 aur 20 ke beech ke prime numbers batao.

subject: maths
prompt_en: Are 12 and 18 co-prime?
prompt_hi: Kya 12 aur 18 co-prime hain?
answer: No: they share 2, 3 and 6 as well as 1

subject: maths
prompt_en: Neither 8 nor 15 is prime. Predict: can they still be co-prime?
prompt_hi: Na 8 prime hai na 15. Guess karo: kya yeh phir bhi co-prime ho sakte hain?
answer: Yes: their only common factor is 1

subject: maths
prompt_en: Kriti says, '3 and 12 are co-prime because 3 is prime.' Check.
prompt_hi: Kriti kehti hai, '3 aur 12 co-prime hain kyunki 3 prime hai.' Check karo.
answer: Not co-prime: 3 divides 12, so 3 is a common factor

subject: maths
prompt_en: Which pair is co-prime: 9 and 14, or 9 and 15?
prompt_hi: Kaunsa pair co-prime hai: 9 aur 14, ya 9 aur 15?
answer: 9 and 14; 9 and 15 share the factor 3

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why are two consecutive numbers, like 20 and 21, always co-prime?
prompt_hi: Do lagataar numbers, jaise 20 aur 21, hamesha co-prime kyon hote hain?
answer: Multiples of any number bigger than 1 are at least 2 apart, so no such number can divide two numbers that are only 1 apart; the only common factor is 1

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why can two even numbers never be co-prime?
prompt_hi: Do even numbers kabhi co-prime kyon nahi ho sakte?
answer: Both have 2 as a factor, so they share more than 1

subject: maths
prompt_en: Are 25 and 36 co-prime?
prompt_hi: Kya 25 aur 36 co-prime hain?
answer: Yes: 25 = 5 × 5 and 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 share no factor except 1

subject: maths
prompt_en: A treasure box lock needs two co-prime numbers between 10 and 20, neither of which is prime. Give one pair.
prompt_hi: Ek khazane ke dabbe ka lock aise do co-prime numbers maangta hai jo 10 aur 20 ke beech hon aur dono mein se koi prime na ho. Ek pair batao.
answer: 14 and 15 (or 15 and 16)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Use factor lists as two circles to show whether 10 and 21 are co-prime.
prompt_hi: Factors ki do circles banakar dikhao ki 10 aur 21 co-prime hain ya nahi.
answer: 10: 1, 2, 5, 10; 21: 1, 3, 7, 21; only 1 is in the overlap, so they are co-prime

subject: maths
prompt_en: Teach a friend what 'co-prime' means, using an example where neither number is prime.
prompt_hi: Dost ko 'co-prime' ka matlab sikhao, aise example se jisme koi bhi number prime na ho.
answer: Two numbers are co-prime if their only common factor is 1, e.g. 8 and 9: 8 has 1, 2, 4, 8 and 9 has 1, 3, 9

subject: maths
prompt_en: Quick! What is the only common factor of two co-prime numbers?
prompt_hi: Jaldi! Do co-prime numbers ka ek hi common factor kaunsa hota hai?

subject: maths
prompt_en: Write 12 as a product of primes.
prompt_hi: 12 ko primes ke product ke roop mein likho.

subject: maths
prompt_en: Write 60 as a product of primes.
prompt_hi: 60 ko primes ke product ke roop mein likho.

subject: maths
prompt_en: Break 360, the degrees in a full turn, into primes.
prompt_hi: 360, yaani full turn ke degrees, ko primes mein todo.

subject: maths
prompt_en: A factor tree for 72 says: 72 = 8 × 9, so the prime factorisation is 8 × 9. What is missing?
prompt_hi: 72 ka factor tree kehta hai: 72 = 8 × 9, toh prime factorisation 8 × 9 hai. Kya chhoot gaya?
answer: 8 and 9 are not prime; split further: 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3

subject: maths
prompt_en: Riya starts 36 as 4 × 9, and Aman starts as 6 × 6. Predict: will they end with the same primes?
prompt_hi: Riya 36 ko 4 × 9 se shuru karti hai, aur Aman 6 × 6 se. Guess karo: kya dono ko same primes milenge?
answer: Yes: both get 2 × 2 × 3 × 3

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why do different factor trees for the same number always end with the same primes?
prompt_hi: Ek hi number ke alag-alag factor trees hamesha same primes pe kyon khatam hote hain?
answer: Every number has exactly one set of prime factors; different trees just find the same primes in a different order

subject: maths
prompt_en: I wrote 15 = 1 × 3 × 5 as its prime factorisation. Is anything wrong?
prompt_hi: Maine 15 ka prime factorisation 15 = 1 × 3 × 5 likha. Kuch galat hai?
answer: Yes: 1 is not prime, so it should be 15 = 3 × 5

subject: maths
prompt_en: Write 84 as a product of primes.
prompt_hi: 84 ko primes ke product ke roop mein likho.

subject: maths
prompt_en: A mela stall has 120 bangles to pack equally into boxes. Using 120 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 5, could boxes of 9 work? Boxes of 8?
prompt_hi: Mele ki ek stall pe 120 chudiyan hain jinhe dabbon mein barabar bharna hai. 120 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 se batao, kya 9-9 ke dabbe chalenge? 8-8 ke?
answer: 9 does not work (9 = 3 × 3 needs two 3s, but 120 has one); 8 works (2 × 2 × 2), giving 15 boxes

subject: maths
prompt_en: Using prime factors, are 45 and 77 co-prime? Are 45 and 75?
prompt_hi: Prime factors se batao, kya 45 aur 77 co-prime hain? 45 aur 75?
answer: 45 = 3 × 3 × 5 and 77 = 7 × 11 share no prime: co-prime. 75 = 3 × 5 × 5 shares 3 and 5 with 45: not co-prime

subject: maths
prompt_en: Teach a friend how to make a factor tree, and how they know when to stop.
prompt_hi: Dost ko sikhao factor tree kaise banate hain, aur kab rukna hai yeh kaise pata chale.
answer: Split the number into any two factors, keep splitting any composite branch, stop when every leaf is prime (never use 1), then multiply back to check
